clue.text: Story that's not told generally

parts.note: a story not told in general terms is one given with every particular spelled out, a full and specific narrative

explanation.surface: A tale that is kept quiet rather than spread about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not told generally' suggests a secret, but it means not told in general terms: a narrative full of specifics.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative given in full particulars is the opposite of a general summary.

clue.text: Straight talking?

parts.note: straight is read as direct and talking as speech, giving the grammatical term for quoting someone's actual words

explanation.definitionFit: The grammar term for reporting a speaker's exact words is read literally as frank, plain utterance.

clue.text: Shakespearean victim once included

indicators.note: the answer is included within the run of letters spanning the words victim and once

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean character who was once a victim is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' tells you to look inside 'victim once', across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens is the title figure of a Shakespeare play, a Shakespearean character.

clue.text: Late stormy rain builds up

indicators.note: stormy suggests wild turbulence, so the letters of rain are tossed into a new order

parts.note: to rear is to build up or raise, as in rearing a structure

explanation.surface: Late in the day, heavy rain gathers into a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' is the anagram signal for the rain; 'Late' means overdue on payments, not tardy or deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: Payments behind schedule are said to be overdue, which is the sense of the phrase.

clue.text: One who is out before his time

definitions.text: One who is out before his time

parts.words: One who is out before his time
parts.note: the surface suggests someone ahead of their era, but a prisoner out before serving his full sentence is meant

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has broken out of prison is free before his sentence ends.

clue.text: A stake on the French evangelist

parts.note: a stake is a post driven into the ground
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone bets on the French preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stake' looks like a bet but is a wooden post.
explanation.definitionFit: A missionary or early preacher of the gospel, as the first followers of Christ were.

clue.text: Plants to go on stage in the Channel Islands

indicators.note: in places the stage piece within the abbreviation for the islands

parts.note: CI is the standard abbreviation for the Channel Islands
to act is to perform on stage

explanation.surface: Someone takes to the theatre in Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands (Jersey, Guernsey and others) between Britain and France abbreviate to CI.
explanation.definitionFit: Succulent spiny plants of desert regions, plural of the familiar prickly pot plant.

clue.text: Partnerships but not companies are boundless

definitions.meaning: in traditional business law partners carry liability without limit, whereas companies usually have limited liability

explanation.surface: A remark on business forms: partnerships, unlike companies, have no limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Liability without a cap describes ordinary partnerships, and without limit also simply means infinite.

clue.text: Rugby physician had a dance

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree, standing for a physician

explanation.surface: A rugby team's doctor took a turn on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance with a distinctive hip movement.

clue.text: Only the second half of the selection first was made with care

indicators.note: first says the selection piece is placed before the other piece

parts.note: a choice is a selection

indicators.note: only the latter half of the letters of the word Only is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions to choose carefully, picking just half of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CHOICE (selection) first, then LY, the second half of 'Only'.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a carefully chosen, discerning manner.

clue.text: Pretty romantic food container

definitions.meaning: describes an idealised, sentimental prettiness like pictures on sweet packaging

explanation.surface: A charming, sweet receptacle for treats.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for twee picturesque scenes comes from the pictures on confectionery packaging, which is also literally a sweets carton.

clue.text: Able to dance a spell

parts.note: if you can do something, you are able
to trip is to dance lightly, as in tripping the light fantastic

explanation.surface: Someone capable of dancing a magic spell.
explanation.walkthrough: A cantrip is a Scottish word for a magic spell or charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a witch's charm or incantation.

clue.text: Hit rump unexpectedly with great success

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals that the letters of hit and rump come out in a surprising rearrangement

explanation.surface: Smacking someone's behind turns out remarkably well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges HIT RUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A victory or outstanding achievement.

clue.text: Endlessly view a part of an opera

indicators.note: endlessly means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: a scene is a view or vista

explanation.surface: An endless view in part of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the last letter from SCENE (view), giving SCEN; add A.
explanation.definitionFit: An elaborate dramatic solo in an opera, an operatic scene.

clue.text: Listen behind a door to first lady's said fall

indicators.note: said means the possessive of Eve is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible, so the first lady's is Eve's
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A secret listener at a doorway, linked to Eve and the Fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' is Eve, not a president's wife; 'said' makes EVE'S sound like EAVES (roof edges).
explanation.definitionFit: To listen secretly to a private conversation, as through a closed door.

clue.text: Forceful measure to get in little by little

annotationWithheld.clue: Forceful measure to get in little by little

clue.text: Downy fibre on weapon first producing deadly mixture

indicators.note: first says the weapon piece leads, with the fibre placed after it

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
cotton is the soft fibre from the cotton plant's seed pods

explanation.surface: Combining soft fibre with a weapon gives something lethal.
explanation.walkthrough: Guncotton is an explosive made by treating cotton with nitric acid.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive compound of nitrated cellulose, a lethal preparation.

clue.text: Imagined face appearing in goal

indicators.note: appearing in means one piece shows up within the other

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
visage is a literary word for face

explanation.surface: Someone pictured a face showing up in the goalmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' suggests football, but it is END, an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictured in the mind or foreseen.

clue.text: Affected fellow, a slippery customer

parts.note: a gent is a man or fellow
an eel is the proverbially slippery fish

explanation.surface: A pretentious man who is not to be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' here means mannered, putting on refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-refined or pretentiously polite, putting on airs.

clue.text: Ambassador drops the first certificate

indicators.note: drops means a letter is removed from the synonym

parts.note: an ambassador is a diplomat

indicators.note: the first refers to the opening letter of the word the

explanation.surface: An envoy leaves behind his first qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: DIPLOMAT (ambassador) loses T, the first letter of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A document awarded on completing a course of study.

clue.text: An old curiosity of a swelling

indicators.note: a curiosity is an oddity, so the letters of an old are made strange by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Echoes Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop, as if describing an antique lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiosity' signals the anagram of AN OLD, punning on Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knob or swelling, and the adjective means relating to one.

clue.text: It is not hard to find it in a chair

definitions.text: It is not hard to find it in a chair

parts.words: It is not hard to find it in a chair
parts.note: reads as saying something is easy to locate, but means a soft thing found on a seat

explanation.definitionFit: A soft pad on a seat, something that is literally not hard.

clue.text: Added photo to introduce right away

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is taken out of the synonym

parts.note: to insert is to introduce something into

explanation.surface: A picture was added to bring something in immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but means R removed: INSERT becomes INSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picture set within a larger one on a page.

clue.text: Stay with the other forward-looking person

parts.note: a prop is a support or stay

indicators.note: other suggests the word the in a different form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A support with something else, looking ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' is an unusual anagram signal: another form of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer who foretells the future.

clue.text: Meet one inside stamping-ground

indicators.note: inside places the single letter within the other piece

parts.note: a meet is a gathering of a fox hunt, so meet stands for hunt
A stands for one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Meeting someone on familiar territory.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hunting a 'meet' is the gathering of a hunt; A for 'one' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite place one frequents, a regular stamping-ground.

clue.text: In favour of prose version by Shakespearean

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: a version of the word prose is a reworked arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Supporting a prose version of a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' is the anagram signal; 'Shakespearean' is the definition, the magician of The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: The magician in The Tempest is a Shakespearean character.

clue.text: Request lift from Tom perhaps

definitions.meaning: to ask for a ride by holding out a hand at the roadside
Tom of the fairy tale, the tiny boy no bigger than a digit

explanation.surface: Asking for a ride from a man named Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchhikers hold out this digit to beg a lift, and Tom of the folk tale bears it as his surname.

clue.text: Belfast to profit with reportedly large amounts of duty?

parts.note: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, an example of a capital
gain is profit

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like stacks when spoken

parts.note: stacks are large amounts, as in stacks of money

explanation.surface: Belfast making profit along with heaps of duty owed.
explanation.walkthrough: Belfast is an example of a capital city; STAX sounds like 'stacks'. The question mark flags this tax as a sort of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy on profits from selling assets, a kind of government charge.
